key_insight: A randomized controlled study at ICLR 2025 found that LLM-generated feedback makes peer reviews more informative and boosts reviewer–author engagement, showing LLMs can effectively augment the peer-review process.
problem_solved: Addresses inconsistent review quality and limited reviewer bandwidth by providing scalable, constructive feedback that improves review usefulness and stimulates productive author–reviewer interaction.
method: Large-scale randomized controlled trial at a major ML conference: reviewers were randomly assigned to receive LLM-generated feedback or not.
LLM outputs were used as reviewer-augmentation (suggestions, clarifications, or draft improvements) rather than replacing reviewers.
Outcomes measured included review informativeness and reviewer–author engagement (e.g., responses, revisions, perceived helpfulness).
impact: Shows a practical, evidence-backed pathway to improve peer review efficiency and quality at scale—useful for conferences, journals, and platforms seeking to augment reviewers without removing human judgment.
visual_elements: Experiment flow diagram: random assignment → reviewer workflows (with vs. without LLM feedback) → outcome measurement

paper_title: A large-scale randomized study of large language model feedback in peer review
paper_authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng
